MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 23, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on May 23, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 19, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Council Member Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

ADDITION OF A LATE ARISING ITEM RELATING TO PROPOSED CONSTITU-
TIONAL AMENDMENT 15 (ACA 15) REGARDING PENSION MANAGEMENT

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff is recommending that the Council add an item to
the agenda to address Mayor Bucknum’s attendance, on behalf of the City of Mission Viejo, at a
meeting in Sacramento May 24, 2017, for the purpose of supporting proposed Constitutional
Amendment (ACA 15) which focusses on public pensions. City Attorney Curley noted that this
matter did not come to the City's attention until Friday last week, subsequent to the posting of the
agenda.

City Council Minutes  1  May 23, 2017
 Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to declare the need to
consider a matter regarding Assembly Constitutional Amendment 15 (ACA 15) which arose
subsequent to the posting of the Agenda and to affirm that the matter must be considered before
the next meeting with the recommendation that it be addressed under Staff Reports tonight.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators. Property: APN 808-720-07, APN 808-
  571-01, APN 808-720-08, APN 808-720-09, APN 808-720-10, APN 808-720-11, APN
  808-720-12, APN 808-132-16. Agency Negotiators: City Manager Wilberg; Assistant
  City Manager Rattay; Community Development Director Lister; Administrative
  Services Director Dyas, City Attorney. Negotiating Parties: NGP Realty. Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel; Initiation of Litigation pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision 54956.9 (1 potential case).

CS3. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member
Kelley was absent.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed three Closed Session items for
which they received updates and provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

David Anderson, Saddleback College, M.V.: announced that the City of Mission Viejo was
honored as “Sponsor of the Year” at last week’s Angels for the Arts Student Success Showcase
City Council Minutes  2  May 23, 2017
 and he said that Saddleback College is grateful for the City’s partnership. Mr. Anderson also
announced three upcoming Summer Theater events that the College and City are co-sponsoring:
Shrek the Musical, The Music Man, Shakespeare on the Green, and a Big Band performance
featuring 100 year-old singer Shep Shepherd.

Claude Parrish, Orange County Tax Assessor: thanked the Mayor and members of the City Council
for making space available at Mission Viejo city hall for a South County Assessor's office. He said
he wanted to open this new office to bring service to South County residents so they don’t have to
endure heavy traffic to Santa Ana.

CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Minutes for the regular meeting of May 9, 2017, as presented.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

City Council Minutes  5  May 23, 2017

City Council Minutes  6  May 23, 2017
 23.  Public Pool and Equipment Room Maintenance Services and Repairs for City

OLD BUSINESS

24.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation - CIP 14325 ~ Restroom and Diving Pits

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1)
  approve Contract Amendment No. 4 to Construct 1 One Corp., in an amount not to exceed
  $89,844.55 for the installation of the Diving Pits; (2) adopt Resolution 17-20 Amending
  CIP 14325 Marguerite Aquatics Complex Budget by $273,153; (3) authorize the Mayor to
  sign the Nadadores Conditional Funding Agreement for the Diving Pits and related
  improvements; and (4) award a contract to Public Restroom Company and issue a Purchase
  Order in an amount not to exceed $133,308.00 pending City Manager and City Attorney
  approval of the jurisdictional venue.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None

City Council Minutes  7  May 23, 2017

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

27.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

28.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

29.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

Agenda item added: Proposed Constitutional Amendment 15 (ACA 15) Regarding Pension
Reform

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that at the beginning of the meeting, the Council voted to
add this item to the agenda.

City Manager Wilberg said that Assemblyman Bill Brough has requested that Mayor Bucknum be
present in Sacramento tomorrow to speak in support of Assembly Constitutional Amendment 15
and to discuss the steps Mission Viejo has taken in regards to pensions. Mr. Wilberg emphasized
that the ACA 15 proposal is very general in nature and would mandate that any future changes to
the pension program would require voter approval.
City Council Minutes  8  May 23, 2017
 30.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief Shane Sherwood reported on recent events including OCFA’s Open House
  at the Regional Fire Operations and Training Center and the mock DUI program “Every
  Fifteen Minutes Counts" which was presented at Trabuco Hills High School. He also
  provided reminders about wildfire precautions which include trimming vegetation and
  grasses around homes.

31.  Proposed 2017-19 Budget for the City of Mission Viejo

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented an outline of the proposed
  2017-19 Budget.

  By consensus, the City Council received the proposed 2017-19 Budget and formally set a
  budget workshop date for Tuesday, June 13, 2017, at 6:00 p.m.

32.  Property Condition Litigation Report - 24331 Augustin, Mission Viejo

  City Attorney Bill Curley noted that the City seldom addresses litigation matters however
  this memo is presented to note the City's position in response to recent comments that he
  believes were incorrect.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the memo by Attorney Curley was written for public
  consumption and to control public thought. She said it fails on all fronts to develop a full
  and fair record.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

33.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reported on the Mission Viejo Nadadores Foundation Spring Soiree at
Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club which was a fundraiser to support the Nadadores portion of the
renovation costs of the Marguerite Aquatics Center. He said it was a great night with a wonderful
guest speaker, Olympic Champion Janet Evans, and he is looking forward to attending again on
an annual basis.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley was absent.

City Council Minutes  9  May 23, 2017
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that the Rotary Club’s Texas Hold ‘Em fundraiser which was
scheduled for June 10, 2017, has been rescheduled for February 24, 2018. He discussed his
attendance at the Santa Margarita Water District and Moulton Niguel Water District Water
Festivals where he learned that despite a winter full of rain, residents are still asked to conserve
water. Council Member Raths also discussed his attendance at a Town Hall meeting presented by
Supervisors Bartlett and Spitzer and Congressman Dana Rohrabacher concerning noise from
airliners taking early turns over the cities of Laguna Niguel and Laguna Beach. He said there is a
proposal to require that planes fly out over the ocean for a longer period of time before they turn
back over populated areas. Lastly, Council Member Raths discussed his attendance at the Mission
Viejo High School 50th anniversary dinner dance where he sat with a group of people from the
class of 1970 and, he said, it was a very enjoyable evening.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Council Member Sachs noted that the City of Mission Viejo pays for 13 crossing guards within
Capistrano Unified School District and 24 in Saddleback Valley Unified School District. He said
commitments like that are over and above the norm and separate Mission Viejo from other cities.
Council Member Sachs stated that Lieutenant Binning has done an extraordinary job keeping crime
low in Mission Viejo but there are more and more reports on the failings of Proposition 47 and
how it has affected some areas. He discussed an article in the Orange County Register that reported
on a family and some doctors who were falsifying urine tests for sober living home residents and
he said the problems with sober living homes are rampant. While Mission Viejo is fortunate to
have fewer sober living homes than some communities, the issue is something that the City needs
to pay attention to. Council Member Sachs discussed his visit with the top hazmat team in Orange
County, noting that they are ready for anything and he also announced that Orange County Fire
Authority’s Academy 44 will graduate on June 28. He encouraged residents to go and witness
how cool a fire academy graduation is.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announced that tonight, the Capistrano Unified School District Board of Trustees
appointed Mission Viejo resident and Community Services Commissioner Judy Bullockus to serve
as the CUSD Area 7 Trustee in an interim capacity. She invited residents to the City’s Memorial
Day ceremony at 8:30 a.m. on May 29 in the Kershaw Garden to honor those that have given so
much for the country. Mayor Bucknum thanked Council Member Raths for engaging in the airport
meetings and noted that Mission Viejo staff has also been monitoring the situation and will
continue to do so on behalf of the residents. She congratulated Tod Burnett who retired as President
of Saddleback College and noted that she presented a certificate to Mr. Burnett on May 10 at his
last Board Meeting. Mayor Bucknum thanked Rancho Mission Viejo for helping to get the rental
fee waived for the Nadadores Spring Soiree event which helped the Nadadores raise more money,
and she also thanked Council Member Kelley for representing the City at the South County Senior
Summit and Council Member Goodell for covering for her at the Bathgate Elementary School flag
ceremony. Mayor Bucknum said that she had a great time at the Mission Viejo High School 50th
City Council Minutes  10  May 23, 2017
 anniversary celebration and at the Orange County Walk for a Cure where 250 participants strode
to raise awareness for a disease that is a very rare food allergy. A Mission Viejo resident has
children with this condition and Mayor Bucknum highlighted that the City is available to help with
these kinds of efforts to bring awareness to good causes.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:59 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 13, 2017, at 6:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 13, 2017
